questions.text: Which of these costs should an emergency fund cover?

options.text: Repairs after your car breaks down
A vacation you've booked for next summer
The down payment on your first home

questions.explanation: An emergency fund is money set aside for costs you can't plan, such as a car repair after a breakdown or a sudden loss of income. A booked vacation and a down payment are planned costs, so you save for them separately.

questions.text: What usually happens if you pay only the minimum on your credit card each month?

options.text: You pay interest for much longer
You pay a late fee each month

questions.explanation: The minimum payment covers the month's interest and only a small part of what you owe. The balance shrinks slowly, so you pay interest for much longer. Only paying the full balance avoids interest, and a late fee applies when you miss the minimum payment or pay it late.

questions.text: How does compound interest grow your savings?

options.text: You earn interest on your deposits and on past interest
You earn interest only on the money you first saved
Your interest rate rises each year you leave the money in

questions.explanation: Each time interest is paid, it is added to your savings, and the next interest is worked out on that larger amount. The rate can stay the same the whole time. Interest worked out only on the money you first saved is simple interest.
